question:
DRAG DROP -
An engineer is implementing security on the Cisco MDS 9000 switch.
Drag and drop the descriptions from the left onto the correct security features on the right.
bank: can be distributed via fabric services
uses the Exchange Fabric Membership Data protocol
allows a preconfigured set of Fibre Channel devices to logically connect to SAN ports
prevent unauthorized switches from joining the fabric or disrupting current fabric operations
theory: Fabric binding and port security are complementary but independent Cisco MDS security features with distinct mechanics: fabric binding operates at the switch level using the Exchange Fabric Membership Data (EFMD) protocol to keep an identical authorized-switch list on every switch, and it cannot be distributed via CFS - it must be configured manually on each switch. Port security instead binds individual devices (Nx ports via pWWN/nWWN) or switches (xE ports via sWWN) to specific interfaces, and unlike fabric binding, its database CAN be distributed through CFS. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 20 - Fabric Binding vs. Port Security)
